title: Mafe Lamb
subtitle: West African lamb stew with peanut sauce and sweet potato
excerpt: Mafe is a rich West African peanut stew from Senegal and Mali. Tender lamb is slow-braised in a peanut and tomato sauce with sweet potato and carrot. It is warming, deeply satisfying food -- substantial enough for a winter main course.
sourceNotes: Mafe -- also spelled maafe or tigadegena (peanut butter stew) -- is one of the most important dishes of Senegambian and Malian cooking. It has spread across the Sahel region and into Guinea, Burkina Faso, and Ivory Coast. Each version varies in the protein used and the level of heat.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 2 months. Reheat gently and stir well.

content.text: Use unsweetened smooth peanut butter. Stir it into warm stock before adding to the pot -- this prevents it from clumping. Sweet potato is sweeter than regular potato here, which balances the richness of the peanut sauce.

items.prepNote: peeled and cut into thick pieces
use 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed

content.text: Season the lamb with salt. Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over high heat. Brown the lamb in batches for 4 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 7 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes and chilli flakes. Cook for 8 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Whisk the peanut butter into 200ml of the warm stock until smooth. Pour into the pot along with the remaining stock.
Return the lamb. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 40 minutes.
Add the carrots and sweet potato. Cover and cook for another 25 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the lamb falls apart.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve with rice.

items.cause: Peanut butter was not dissolved before adding
items.fix: Always whisk peanut butter into warm stock first, then pour into the pot

items.symptom: Lamb is still tough after 40 minutes
items.fix: Continue cooking on low heat for another 20 minutes; lamb shoulder becomes tender slowly
Add the sweet potato only in the last 25 minutes of cooking

content.text: Mafe is at the heart of Senegalese cooking and is one of the dishes most associated with the Senegambian region. In Senegal it is often made with mutton or goat and served at large family gatherings. The dish has travelled widely across West Africa through trade and migration, and is now found from Mauritania to Ivory Coast.
